# Plan: Build a Prismic Website with Next.js

## 1. Define the website

Before coding, document:

- Required pages and routes
- Primary audiences and user journeys
- Navigation structure
- SEO requirements
- Responsive breakpoints
- Accessibility expectations
- Content ownership and publishing workflow

Use Next.js App Router, which provides file-based routing, layouts, Server Components, and modern rendering patterns. [Next.js App Router documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app)

## 2. Create the Next.js project

Set up a TypeScript Next.js application with:

- App Router
- ESLint
- Tailwind CSS or another design system
- Image optimization
- A shared `src/` structure
- Environment variables for Prismic configuration

Current Next.js documentation lists Node.js 20.9 as the minimum requirement for new projects. [Next.js installation guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)

Suggested structure:

```text
src/
  app/
    layout.tsx
    page.tsx
    [...uid]/
      page.tsx
    api/
  components/
  lib/
  slices/
  styles/
```

## 3. Create and configure the Prismic repository

Create a Prismic repository and connect it to the project using:

- `@prismicio/client`
- `@prismicio/react`
- `@prismicio/next`
- Slice Machine

Prismic’s Slice Machine setup supports an official Next.js adapter and can generate the core configuration and dependencies. [Prismic Slice Machine documentation](https://prismic.io/docs/technical-reference/slice-machine-ui)

Configure:

- Repository name
- API endpoint
- Preview references
- Environment variables
- Local Slice Machine development
- Production deployment settings

## 4. Design the content model

Create content types based on editorial needs rather than directly copying page layouts.

Typical custom types:

- `Page`
  - Title
  - SEO fields
  - Hero content
  - Slice Zone
- `Article` or `Blog Post`
  - Title
  - Author
  - Publication date
  - Featured image
  - Categories
  - Body content
- `Author`
- `Category`
- `Settings`
  - Site title
  - Logo
  - Navigation
  - Footer links
  - Social links

Use relationships for reusable entities such as authors and categories. Keep global settings separate from page content.

## 5. Build the Slice library

Create reusable slices such as:

- Hero
- Rich text section
- Image and text
- Feature grid
- Testimonials
- Logo strip
- Call to action
- FAQ
- Article listing
- Contact form
- Video or embed section

Each slice should include:

- A clear content model
- A React component
- Responsive styling
- Accessibility considerations
- Empty and fallback states
- A preview in Slice Machine

Render slices through a central resolver so editors can compose pages without requiring a developer for every layout change.

## 6. Implement routing and rendering

Use a dynamic route for Prismic pages:

```text
app/[...uid]/page.tsx
```

The route should:

1. Read the requested UID.
2. Query Prismic.
3. Render the page’s Slice Zone.
4. Return a 404 page if no document exists.
5. Generate page metadata from Prismic SEO fields.

Use static generation or cached server rendering for public pages, with revalidation when content changes. Keep interactive features—forms, menus, carousels, and filters—in client components only where needed.

## 7. Add previews and editorial workflow

Implement Prismic previews so editors can view unpublished changes inside the website.

Include:

- Preview route
- Draft mode handling
- Preview ref support
- Exit-preview control
- Slice Machine simulator
- Clear local development instructions

This allows content editors to validate pages before publishing.

## 8. Add SEO and accessibility

Implement:

- Dynamic `<title>` and description metadata
- Open Graph and Twitter metadata
- Canonical URLs
- XML sitemap
- `robots.txt`
- Structured data where appropriate
- Semantic HTML
- Keyboard navigation
- Visible focus states
- Alt text requirements
- Good color contrast
- Correct heading hierarchy

Use Prismic image fields and Next.js image handling to generate responsive, optimized images.

## 9. Build shared site functionality

Create reusable components for:

- Header and navigation
- Mobile menu
- Footer
- Breadcrumbs
- Buttons and links
- Rich text rendering
- Error and loading states
- Cookie or privacy controls
- Form validation and submission

Keep site-wide navigation and footer data in the `Settings` document so editors can manage them centrally.

## 10. Test the website

Test at several levels:

- Unit tests for utility functions
- Component tests for important slices
- Integration tests for Prismic queries
- End-to-end tests for navigation, forms, and preview mode
- Responsive testing
- Accessibility testing
- Browser testing
- Content edge cases such as missing images or empty slices

Also test published and unpublished content separately.

## 11. Deploy

Deploy the Next.js application to a hosting platform such as Vercel or another Node-compatible provider.

Configure:

- Production environment variables
- Preview deployments
- Prismic webhook-triggered revalidation
- Custom domain
- HTTPS
- Analytics
- Error monitoring
- Caching strategy

The deployment should support both normal published requests and Prismic preview requests.

Before launch:

- Populate realistic content
- Review all routes and redirects
- Run Lighthouse and accessibility checks
- Verify metadata and sitemap output
- Test forms and integrations
- Confirm editorial permissions
- Create a content editing guide

After launch, monitor:

- Build failures
- Runtime errors
- Slow pages
- Broken links
- Search performance
- Content publishing issues
- Webhook and preview behavior
